formulas.name: Node connectivity (Whitney 1932)
formulas.latex: \kappa(G)=\min_{s,t\text{ non-adjacent}}\kappa(s,t)\qquad(\kappa(K_n)=n-1)

formulas.name: Approximation (White and Newman 2001)
formulas.latex: \tilde\kappa(s,t)=\#\text{paths found by repeatedly taking a shortest }s\text{-}t\text{ path and deleting its inner nodes}
formulas.where: A lower bound \(\tilde\kappa(s,t)\le\kappa(s,t)\) obtained greedily; the graph value is the minimum over pairs (or over the sampled pairs), so it is an upper-bounded estimate and not exact. The result depends on which shortest path is chosen at each step.

variants.ap_node_connectivity: The greedy node-disjoint-path approximation of the node connectivity of the whole network: a lower bound on \(\kappa(G)\) per pair, depending on the order of the search.

formulas.name: Minimum s-t cut (Ford and Fulkerson 1956)
formulas.latex: \min_{S\ni s,\,t\notin S}w(S,V\setminus S)=\max\text{ flow value from }s\text{ to }t
formulas.where: Capacity of a smallest cut separating the source side from the sink side; equal to the maximum flow. The cut set is not unique: the source-side set of minimal and of maximal size differ.

formulas.name: Global minimum cut (Stoer and Wagner 1997)
formulas.latex: \min_{\emptyset\ne S\subsetneq V}w(S,V\setminus S)
formulas.where: Smallest cut over all bipartitions of an undirected weighted graph; 0 for a disconnected graph; needs \(n\ge2\).

formulas.name: Cut measures of a node-set pair
formulas.latex: \mathrm{cutsize}=w(S,T),\ \ \mathrm{ncut}=\tfrac{w(S,T)}{\mathrm{vol}(S)}+\tfrac{w(S,T)}{\mathrm{vol}(T)},\ \ \phi=\tfrac{w(S,T)}{\min(\mathrm{vol}(S),\mathrm{vol}(T))},\ \ h=\tfrac{w(S,T)}{\min(|S|,|T|)}
formulas.where: Cut size, normalized cut (Shi and Malik 2000), conductance (Kannan, Vempala and Vetta 2004), edge expansion for node sets \(S\) and \(T\); undefined when a volume or size is 0.

formulas.name: Minimum edge cut
formulas.latex: F^\star\in\arg\min\{|F|:F\subseteq E,\ G-F\ \text{disconnected}\},\qquad|F^\star|=\lambda(G)
formulas.where: A smallest set of edges whose removal disconnects the graph (or separates \(s\) from \(t\) in the \(s\)-\(t\) form, with \(|F|=\lambda(s,t)\) by Menger). The set is not unique; its size is. A disconnected graph has the empty cut.

variants.edge_cut: A minimum edge cut of the whole graph: its size is \(\lambda(G)\), the particular set is one of the minimum cuts.
variants.st_edge_cut: A minimum \(s\)-\(t\) edge cut between node 0 and node \(n-1\) as pairs of ends.

formulas.name: Minimum node cut
formulas.latex: X^\star\in\arg\min\{|X|:X\subseteq V,\ G-X\ \text{disconnected}\},\qquad|X^\star|=\kappa(G)
formulas.where: A smallest set of nodes whose removal disconnects the graph, or (\(s\)-\(t\) form) separates \(s\) from \(t\) with \(|X|=\kappa(s,t)\) for non-adjacent \(s,t\). Not defined for a complete graph, and no \(s\)-\(t\) node cut exists for adjacent nodes. The set is not unique; its size is. A disconnected graph has the empty cut.

variants.st_node_cut: A minimum \(s\)-\(t\) node cut between node 0 and node \(n-1\); none exists when they are adjacent.

notation.meaning: directed graph with a start node \(r\)

immediate dominator: the dominator of \(v\) closest to \(v\), other than \(v\)

formulas.name: Dominators (Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy 2001)
formulas.latex: d\ \mathrm{dom}\ v\iff\text{every path from }r\text{ to }v\text{ contains }d
formulas.where: Defined for nodes reachable from \(r\); \(r\) dominates all and \(\mathrm{idom}(r)=r\) by convention. The immediate dominators form a tree.

formulas.name: Dominance frontier (Cytron et al. 1991)
formulas.latex: \mathrm{DF}(d)=\{v:\exists p\in\mathrm{pred}(v),\ d\ \mathrm{dom}\ p,\ d\ \text{does not strictly dominate}\ v\}
formulas.where: The nodes where the dominance of \(d\) ends.

variants.idom: The immediate dominator of every node reachable from the start (the start's is itself); unreachable nodes get a none mark.
variants.frontiers: The dominance frontier \(\mathrm{DF}(d)\) of every node (a marker for nodes unreachable from the start).

formulas.name: Gomory-Hu tree (Gomory and Hu 1961)
formulas.latex: T\ \text{a tree on }V:\ \lambda(s,t)=\min_{e\in T[s,t]}w_T(e)\ \text{and each tree edge}\ e\text{ defines a minimum cut of value }w_T(e)
formulas.where: A weighted tree that encodes the minimum cut value between every pair as the minimum edge weight on the tree path and also the cuts themselves; \(n-1\) maximum flows build it (Gusfield 1990). An equivalent flow tree keeps only the first property. The tree is not unique, the values it encodes are.

variants.gomory_hu: The edges of a Gomory-Hu tree with their weights (each node's parent and the minimum cut value to it, Gusfield's method); the tree's shape is not unique.
variants.gomory_hu_values: The pairwise minimum cut values \(\lambda(u,v)\) for \(u<v\) that the tree encodes (unique).
variants.cat_equivalent_flow_gusfield_tree: Documented for JGraphT as the Gusfield equivalent flow tree: a tree with the pairwise values as minimum edge weights on paths, without the cut property.

a flow: \(0\le f(e)\le c(e)\), conserved at every node except the source set \(S\) and sink set \(T\)

formulas.name: Maximum flow (Ford and Fulkerson 1956)
formulas.latex: \max_f\ \sum_{e\text{ out of }S}f(e)-\sum_{e\text{ into }S}f(e)\quad\text{s.t. capacity and conservation}
formulas.where: The maximum value equals the minimum cut capacity (max-flow min-cut theorem). The value is unique, the flow on individual edges is not. Algorithms: augmenting paths (Edmonds and Karp 1972), blocking flows (Dinic 1970). A multi-source, multi-sink problem is reduced to one source and one sink with infinite-capacity arcs. An unbounded value results when an \(S\)-\(T\) path has infinite capacity.

variants.max_flow: The maximum flow value and one flow on every edge (the value is determined, the edge flows are not).
variants.gb_maxflow: The maximum flow value between two nodes on the simple graph with edge weights as capacities.

formulas.name: Minimum-cost flow (Ahuja, Magnanti and Orlin 1993)
formulas.latex: \min_f\sum_ec(e)f(e)\quad\text{s.t. }\ 0\le f(e)\le u(e),\ \ \sum_{e\text{ out of }v}f(e)-\sum_{e\text{ into }v}f(e)=b(v)
formulas.where: A flow meeting all supplies and demands at least cost; infeasible when no such flow exists. Network simplex is due to Dantzig 1951 and Cunningham 1976 for the strongly feasible version. Costs may be negative if there is no negative-cost cycle of unbounded capacity.

variants.max_flow_min_cost: A maximum flow of least cost between two nodes, with its value (the value and cost are determined; the flow is not).
variants.gb_mincost: The minimum cost of sending one unit from node 0 to node \(n-1\) (demand \(-1\) and \(+1\)).
variants.cat_capacity_cost_flow_minimum_scaling: Documented for JGraphT as the capacity scaling algorithm for minimum cost flow.
variants.cat_ahuja_augmentation_cyclic_exchange_l: Documented for JGraphT as the Ahuja-Orlin-Sharma cyclic exchange local augmentation for minimum cost flow.
